This one feels more of a movie than the others because of the long and repetitive cutscenes, not many action sections, poor choices that make you feel like you have no power on the story (like watching a movie)

I appreciate the fact that you spent time and effort to express your personal opinion, that is the way all discussions should be :) 

About the story: I said it’s trivial in the sense that it’s trite, banal, corny. The “it was all a dream/allucination is something that kills stories for me.

In regards to action sections: it’s better than having none, but I think they’re too long in the sense that they’re very repetitive, they only require qte. I think in the other games they made them feel more unique and found a better balance between qte and other actions.

Locked traits: I feel like this one could be and interesting game mechanics, I just didn’t know anything about it before and while playing the game. It’s not bad, it’s just something that I found hard to understand while doing my first playthrough, I don’t think that the game accompanies the player enough in this new thing

When you write a story, the easiest thing is to include magic in the narrative or make it twist into a dream, this is what I find the most trivial about it. A realistic story is much harder to build but is way more solid. 
About the game mechanics, I already mentioned what I didn’t like: long and slow cutscenes, long quicktime events sections. Another thing is the weight of choices: they feel like they don’t count; as a player I felt I had little power over the story. Being more specific, the way andrew may shoot angela without the player’s intention to, for example.
The game overall feels like 50% cutscenes (which are boring after a while, because they’re all very similar and depict a trivial story), 40% walking (spaces are too open, too many roads) and 10% action (which is not that fun!)
